title: The Sick Village
timelinePosition: Two days' ride south of Millhaven (Ch3 closed on the evening of the first day, at the farm with the lit shrine). Arrival late morning; infirmary work through the afternoon; the join at late afternoon; the granary at dusk; the initiate dies in the evening; the shutdown and the ward vigil run through the night; morning departure. Jaina has slept in camp at least once since she slept in the saddle, so she arrives sharp, and the night vigil wears her down again. Mark time by events, not counts (Jaina voice rule).
openLocation: A working village south of Millhaven where people are falling ill but have not named the outbreak
transport: Southbound on Thalassian horses, then on foot inside the village
immediateObjective: Learn how the sickness gets into people quickly enough to keep this village from becoming another Millhaven.
constraints: Absolute limited third on Jaina; nothing she could not perceive or infer
No grain connection before Jaina earns it from the patient pattern (B5); bread smoke and the bakery before then are ambient texture only
No proof of a cult before the granary scene (B8)
No solved old carter mystery; the carter and the newer grain man stay unconnected scraps, and the supplier description in B7 is a resemblance, not an identification
Jaina is never clueless about necromancy: her gap is banned practice, not the field itself

Jaina's narration name for Sylvanas moves from 'Windrunner' (her Ch2 narration: 'Windrunner', 'the Ranger-General', once 'the elf') to 'Sylvanas' across the chapter. The slide comes after B2 and should settle by Scene 3. Aloud she keeps saying 'Ranger-General' all chapter; she does not say 'Sylvanas' aloud yet. She stops talking down to her, and there is no open emotional trust.
Lyriel's switch from 'Lady Proudmoore' to 'Jaina' lands in the knot lesson (B4)
No Barov connection and no concrete recognition of the old carter
Neral and the fourth ranger are gone; the party is exactly four and the empty places are a callback, not a new image
Fatigue from the Ch 2 no-sleep ride has been partly slept off, but the chapter's night work should tire her again
Brask appears last on page here; do not return him

Custody terms from Ch2 still hold: Jaina is a prisoner in the middle of the line. In the village Sylvanas works in pairs (her Ch3 drill), so Lyriel stays with Jaina in the infirmary and Cyndia goes with Sylvanas. The pairing is the custody arrangement, and Jaina may notice it as one.

Jaina's hands are the running cost: as of Ch3 the left is raw and wrapped in linen, the right has been dead since the Ch2 frost-sheet, and Sylvanas banned hand-reading. Do not heal them off-page. Body reads go through spell light and the staff, not deep palm reads. The B9 barrier and the night vigil cost her more, and nothing resets.
Andorhal has never been named on the page. Its first mention needs an in-world source (see B7 and B11a), not a guess from nowhere.
The village stays unnamed (the outline and Brask's voice sheet give it no name). If the writer names it, the memory-keeper must log the name for Brask's Ch23 letter.
Brask's voice-sheet sample 'I sold barley in Millhaven last autumn' is a grain pre-signal; do not use it before B5. In B2 he repeats 'Millhaven.' and nothing grain-related.

povKnowsAtOpen: Millhaven's dead marched north toward Quel'Thalas
Millhaven looks like the first village on this road that was fully lost
Other places can still look ordinary even when the sickness is already rooted in them
Her magical sensitivity lets the party feel trouble earlier than most people would, but at Millhaven it came too late to save anyone
The plague is physical, pervasive, lethal and necromantic in broad Kirin Tor terms, even if the exact banned method sits outside her training
Neral already rode north with the survivor girl and the warning
The old carter on the road and the girl's newer grain man are still only weak clues
povDoesNotKnowAtOpen: How the sickness first gets into the body
Whether this village can still be saved
Whether someone is steering the outbreak or it is spreading on its own
The exact point where sickness becomes undeath
Whether the old carter from the road actually matters
mustNotBeImpliedYet: Grain connection before Jaina earns it from the patient pattern
Proof of a cult before the granary scene
That Jaina knows nothing about necromancy
Concrete recognition of the old carter's identity
Open emotional trust between Jaina and Sylvanas
castKnowsLeavingChapter: Grain carries the plague into people
Roads and storehouses are how the plague spreads
A live watcher was inside the village and died by poison before he could be questioned
The village lives: Brask stopped the grain on their word and the early cases held under Jaina's wards
Andorhal is the next destination on the route
The old carter and the newer grain man are still unresolved scraps

pov: She opens believing that if she can find the entry route fast enough, she can stop this village from becoming another Millhaven.
She keeps reaching for a clean magical answer and underrates Sylvanas's read of people, habits, and supply.
By the end, Jaina has the answer, but it comes through food, labor, timing, and Sylvanas's practical eye as much as through spellwork.
She stops treating Sylvanas like escort muscle and starts bringing the human side of the problem straight to her.
She leaves with a village that lives because they were on time, and with a ranger's knot in her hands that Lyriel taught her.

beats: Jaina starts out reading Sylvanas as sharp, useful, and secondary to the real magical problem.
Sylvanas keeps seeing the pressure points Jaina misses: fear, routine, authority, and supply.
By the end, Jaina is thinking of her as Sylvanas, not just the ranger, and she stops talking down to her.

team.label: Partnership
beats: They enter the village as two specialists on the same road, but not the same method.
The investigation proves neither approach works alone.
They leave still tense, but now they are solving one problem together instead of arguing over whose kind of knowledge counts.
This is their one clean win: on time, and it holds.

castAndHandoffRules: Cyndia: still with the riding party.
Lyriel: still with the riding party. She works the infirmary beside Jaina and teaches her the Farstrider one-handed bandage knot.
Neral: not with the party. She already left north with the survivor girl.

Captain Willem Brask: the village militia captain. He blocks them, yields to Sylvanas, and stops the grain on their word. He does not return on-page. His only later appearance is a sworn letter for the defence in Chapter 23.
Local village cast: the medic, granary keeper, and cult initiate belong to this outbreak site only.
Next chapter starts: Chapter 5 opens with the same four riders following the grain road southwest.

chapterBridge.previousChapterClose: Ch3 ends in Sylvanas's POV on the evening of the first day south: a living farm with smoke, a dog at the gate, a rowan, a lit candle in the gatepost shrine, and a woman who stares at the bows and the mage's hands wrapped in white rags and shuts her door. The staff in the crook of the mage's elbow points past the farm, south, and the dog follows them along the hedge, barking.
chapterBridge.continuityOfState: Two days' ride later, same four riders: Sylvanas in front, Cyndia left, Lyriel right, Jaina in the middle on the borrowed mare, still a prisoner under the Ch2 terms. Two empty places at the back of the line. Jaina's hands are still wrapped (left raw, right dead since the Ch2 frost-sheet) and hand-reading is banned. She has slept since the saddle-sleep and arrives sharper than she left Millhaven.
chapterBridge.informationAsymmetry: First time inside Jaina since Ch2, and Ch3 showed her only from outside, so her own read of Millhaven is hers to carry in now, without a recap. She knows the girl, the count, the carter's question and the 'wider' reading. Her Ch2 wish to find someone alive was answered by the cellar. She does not know that Sylvanas felt the noon stone or saw the circle on the map, that Sylvanas thought 'Damn her, then' at her refusal, or that Sylvanas is telling herself she follows the trail, not the mage.
chapterBridge.orientingAnchor: One anchor is enough: the staff still pointing south, now at a village with smoke in its chimneys, and the wrongness under ordinary noise. Don't re-run the two days.
chapterBridge.intentionalJump: POV switch (Sylvanas to Jaina) and a time skip of two days' riding.

scene.title: The Granary
scene.sceneFunction: The village investigation turns into an active hunt inside the grain stores, and the village is saved.
scene.knowledgeAtSceneStart: Dusk. Grain, meaning the new supplier's stock, is the carrier, and the granary is where they can prove it. Jaina's stabilization wards are set and left standing over the worst cases while she goes; they weaken without her. The party moves on the granary at once.

beats.goal: Catch whoever is working the granary and keep the evidence intact.
beats.conflict: The young initiate is watching the operation, realizes he is caught and goes for a lamp to burn everything; fire would destroy the proof and the stock.

outcome.summary: Sylvanas stops the fire, Jaina restrains the watcher, and the concentrated liquid shows the poison is made before it reaches the flour; for a moment they hold both a living witness and a fresh crime scene.

beats.valueShift: a theory about grain -> proof of organization
newOnPageInformation: A young initiate was watching the granary operation
The poison exists as a concentrated liquid before it is mixed into flour
The granary is proof of organization instead of accident
sensoryAnchors: clay vessel breaking on floorboards
the wrong sweet smell of the concentrate
Sylvanas's arrow pinning a sleeve instead of a throat
lamp oil
grain-sack dust in the air
beats.transitionIntent: action continuation: the concentrate is spreading across the boards, and the prisoner and the spill both need hands at once
beats.plannerWarning: Cult proof starts here and only here. Jaina's POV: she sees the arrow and the lamp but not Sylvanas's reasoning for the shot. Her restraint of the watcher is magical (a hold or binding) and must not become an evasion of the rule that she is no fighter.
beats.continuityNote: The concentrate's wrong sweetness belongs to the same family as the patients' breath (B3) and the girl's 'pears gone brown'. Jaina can feel the kinship; she does not need to say it. Her restraint is magical (frost or a hold through the staff; frost through the staff is established from the Ch2 ambush) and costs the hands. She is no fighter. Lamp and torch light make sense at dusk.
beats.povNote: Per the action-POV research: tunnel attention and sensation over choreography. She sees the lamp and the arrow strike, not Sylvanas's reasoning for the shot.

beats.goal: Contain the spilled concentrate and learn what it is.
beats.conflict: The initiate is frightened and nearly useless; the spill matters more than his panic, and a slow barrier risks the stock, the floor and the party.

outcome.summary: Jaina contains the liquid fast enough to study it: master-level alchemical work built on necromantic theory she knows only from warnings, so the plague is made, not improvised. The prisoner is too low to explain it and they move him to a cell.

beats.valueShift: evidence in hand -> evidence beyond her training
newOnPageInformation: The concentrate is master-level alchemical work on necromantic theory
The plague is made, not improvised
The prisoner is too low-level to explain much
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Where the centre of the network is
sensoryAnchors: torchlight shaking on the prisoner's face
a barrier thrown over the spill
Cyndia and Lyriel hauling him upright
sweet fumes held down by the ward
beats.transitionIntent: action continuation: they walk him to the militia lockup, and the questioning is next
beats.plannerWarning: Hold back: Jaina knows the field from the outside (banned practice, not the field). She recognizes the design is brilliant and necromantic and that she lacks the frame, per plague-mechanism.md. Do not let her name Kel'Thuzad or a school. Do not suggest she knows nothing about necromancy.
beats.continuityNote: Jaina knows necromancy in broad Kirin Tor terms and lacks the banned frame (plague-mechanism.md: she recognizes brilliance and design early). The barrier over the spill is a hard, fast cast, so the hands pay. The lockup is the village's, which means Brask's key and his militia; his presence from here on is natural.

beats.goal: Question the initiate before anyone else tells him what to say.
beats.conflict: He is already beyond reach: by the time they lock him in, he has swallowed poison meant for capture.

outcome.summary: He dies silent. The watcher was trained to die, and the people behind the plague are organized enough to waste village-level agents. They lose their only direct witness and keep only the route.

beats.valueShift: a living witness -> only the road
newOnPageInformation: The initiate swallowed capture-poison and died before questioning
The group trains its watchers to die silent
The only direct witness is gone
sensoryAnchors: warm body on cold stone
a trace of foam at the mouth
cell bar chill
the room going still
beats.transitionIntent: emotional carryover: beaten to the witness, they carry the loss straight into what they can still do tonight
beats.plannerWarning: Beat them again lightly: this is a loss, not a catastrophe, and the chapter ends in a win. The thought that a faster barrier might have kept him talking belongs to B11, in the night, not here.
beats.continuityNote: This is the first proof of organization. It answers part of Ch3's 'who drives sixty dead up a cow way' only by implication: someone organized trains watchers to die. No commander, no name, no cult name. Plausibility: Jaina's hold binds his body, not his mouth, so the poison can be on him (cheek, collar, hem) and swallowed during the walk. The writer chooses where, but Jaina does not see him take it.

beats.emotion: Tired, wary, beaten to the witness, and still in time if the village moves tonight.
beats.dilemma: Let the village weigh a stranger's word overnight, or press Brask to shut the granary and the ovens and burn the stock now, with the witness dead and the proof a broken jar and a theory from the sickroom.
beats.decision: Brask closes the granary and the bakery on their word, sends riders after the last flour cart and burns the tainted stock in the yard. Jaina goes back to the cots and holds her wards over the sick through the night.
beats.valueShift: beaten to the witness -> acting in time

beats.transitionIntent: intentional hard cut: from the night vigil to morning and the first broken fevers
beats.interiority: the dead initiate, and whether a faster barrier would have kept him talking; the wards are time, not a cure, and time is all she has; checking the fevers again
beats.plannerWarning: Brask gives way completely and moves fast ('Tell me what to shut.' is the shape). Jaina's register to blocking authority is polite and immovable. Who talks to Brask is the writer's call; the arc wants Jaina bringing the people side straight to Sylvanas and Sylvanas reading the authority. Do not add open emotional trust.
beats.continuityNote: The wards were set and left standing while she went to the granary (S3 start). She comes back to them weakened and renews them. A night of holding wards on top of the barrier is a cost on the hands that escalates and does not reset.

beats.emotion: Tired, careful relief: it held, here; it is one village.
beats.dilemma: Stay to see the village through, or take what the village gave them and go after the road.
beats.decision: With the early cases holding and the first fevers broken, they leave Brask to it and take the grain road southwest toward Andorhal.

beats.plannerWarning: Brask appears on page for the last time. His ledger moment is a sworn-record gesture, not a farewell scene, because his Ch23 letter depends on it. He says their names aloud as he writes and asks for the spelling (brask-voice.md). No blessing or ornate farewell from him or anyone (the farewell is the Mal'Ganis tell). No open emotional trust between Jaina and Sylvanas: she thinks 'Sylvanas' now and stops talking down, and the two stay tense. No Barov connection, no carter identity.
beats.continuityNote: Andorhal needs a concrete source on the page by this beat: where the supplier's stock came up from (the granary keeper's account, the tally or marks on the burned sacks, the road the flour cart took, or Brask's knowledge of the grain road). The writer picks one, and it confirms the B7 guess. Millhaven source-or-sink advances: Millhaven was a late stage of a pattern that runs along the grain road, not a lone origin. Ch5 opens on the grain road southwest with the same four riders.

scene.verifierNote: Outline beat 11 is split into B11 (the night: shutdown, burning, vigil) and B11a (the morning: the fevers broken, the ledger, the road). Both carry outlineBeat 11.

factsLocked: Grain is confirmed as the plague carrier.
The village lives. Captain Willem Brask stopped the grain on their word and wrote their names in his ledger.
Jaina can tie the Farstrider one-handed knot Lyriel taught her.
Roads and storehouses are how the plague spreads.
A live watcher existed inside the village and died by poison rather than talk.
The party's next move is to follow the route southwest toward Andorhal.
Millhaven remains the first village fully claimed in the pattern, while other settlements are still in earlier stages.
The old carter and the survivor's newer grain man remain weak but persistent clues.
factsNotEarned: Concrete recognition of the old carter's identity.
Open emotional trust between Jaina and Sylvanas.
